strings.name: Armand Duplantis
strings.role: Athlete · Pole vault world record setter
strings.summary: Raised in a sporting family in Louisiana, Duplantis competes internationally for Sweden. He progressed from youth world champion to Olympic and senior world champion, combining runway speed, coordination and specialized training. He retained Olympic gold in Paris in 2024, won a third outdoor world title in 2025 and cleared a world-record 6.31m in 2026 while adding further global titles.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: An Olympic champion who has repeatedly broken the pole-vault world record, pushing the technical limits of athletics.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Olympic and world titles
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won Olympic gold in Tokyo in 2021 and Paris in 2024, then a third outdoor world title in Tokyo in 2025.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Repeated world records
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: First broke the senior world record in 2020 and raised the bar to 6.31m in Uppsala in March 2026.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: First Ultimate Championship title
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Cleared 6.20m to win the men’s pole vault at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Fourth world indoor title
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Won in Poland with a championship-record 6.25m for a fourth consecutive world indoor title.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: World record of 6.31m
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Cleared 6.31m at the Mondo Classic in Uppsala, adding one centimetre to his world record.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Third outdoor world title and 6.30m
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won his third outdoor world title in Tokyo and improved the then world record to 6.30m.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Retained Olympic gold in Paris
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Won his second Olympic gold and ended the Paris final with a world-record 6.25m.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: First outdoor world title
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Won his first outdoor world title in Oregon after already becoming Olympic and world indoor champion.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Olympic gold in Tokyo
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won with 6.02m at the Tokyo Olympics held in 2021, taking his first Olympic title.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: First senior world records
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Cleared 6.17m in Torun to beat Renaud Lavillenie’s record, then improved to 6.18m in Glasgow a week later.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: European champion and U20 record
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Won the European title in Berlin at eighteen with a world U20 record of 6.05m.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: World youth champion
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Won for Sweden in Cali with 5.30m, a major international youth breakthrough.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Lafayette
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Louisiana and coached by his parents; began vaulting in the family backyard before representing Sweden.
